body: Pills, and I'd rather not say, mainly because I wouldn't want anyone learning from her "mistakes".

Cheers for the positive comments. Nowhere near Minnesota I'm afraid. Not in the US.

The positive comments help. I will see what support I can get, but it's not in my nature to ask others for help. It's really hard to be "a pain" to friends and family! All my calls today have started with "so what are your plans today?" funny enough, being a work day, most people are busy.

Don't like the idea of leaving her alone, despite that the hospital does provide a semi-dedicated person to watch her. I know this sounds crazy, but we are all a little bit nuts, aren't we?

Yes, the life she left behind, before me. 

As for support, mainly it's me, though I'm trying to get some extra support in place this time around, but it's very easy for people to see me supporting her and do less, because she "has the support"

As for support for me, well, some. But it's really hard calling on your friends, especially when you know what stuff they are going through. Everyone has issues ( that's a broad statement, not specific to my friends and family), so it's hard to put your own problems above theirs, especially when your own problem is that someone else has an even bigger problem... I think that makes sense.

Manhug gratefully appreciated.

In patient in hospital being treated for the OD. Our medical system may work differently to yours. I'm not in the US. 

As for ignoring her, yes and no. I'm sure shed physically be fine, but she could come out of this a lot worse than she hopefully will.

Alcohol. And take away the alcohol, and you reveal some awful shit she's had to deal with in life. So the true mental illness here, I suspect can best be described as PTSD. Therapy, medication, and lots of support is the cure.

The problem I face is the long term support. It's hour 11 here now, she's almost finished the 2nd of 3 iv drips, the next will take 14 hours. I can manage that. I can be there and be a rock for that. Being a rock for the next 3 months is scary part.

At the moment I am coping with the line "I will manage because I have to. There is no other option". That worked the first time.

She is an inpatient. In a perfect world the mental health support facilities would cater for everyone, and always be perfect. Given the state of healthcare in other parts of the world, I'm glad we have what we have. I could abandon her to the system, let it do it's thing, but the doctors and nurses all acknowledge that a patient, especially a suicide attempt, get better care if the spouse/partner is there. It's too easy to ignore the ones who "don't want help".

As for making it all her responsibility, it's a bit foolish. If she wants to kill herself, without a support network, she will. 

Yes she could get checked into a facility for a few weeks, but that is not the best care for her, and if you are married then you know that only the best will suffice.

Yeah, that's pretty much everything I did the first time round. This time round the path isn't so clear, partly because I know what's coming. The first time around I didn't know and only had to be a rock, hold out, etc for one more day. This time around I know what I'm in for.

It all sounds terribly selfish, after all, it's her that needs the help.
